title: Duplicate 'Error:' prefix in displayed error message
claim: The template literal `Error: ${e}` results in double 'Error:' because standard Error objects already include the 'Error:' prefix in their toString output.
evidence: `errorDiv.textContent = `Error: ${e}`;` When `e` is an Error instance, `String(e)` is `Error: <message>`, so final string is `Error: Error: <message>`.
trigger: Any runtime error is caught and displayed.
impact: Minor user-facing message quality issue; users see redundant prefix.
test_implication: Manual testing of error display will show duplicated prefix; unit test can simulate error object and inspect textContent.
suggested_verification: Trigger an error and inspect the rendered error div; observe double 'Error:'.
suggested_fix: Change to `errorDiv.textContent = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e);` or `errorDiv.textContent = `${e.name}: ${e.message}`;` if error object.

title: Stack trace line breaks lost in error display
claim: The stack trace is displayed in a `div` without `white-space: pre-wrap` or similar, causing newline characters to collapse to spaces, making the stack unreadable.
evidence: `const stackDiv = document.createElement('div'); ... stackDiv.textContent = `Stack: ${e.stack}`;` No white-space style set; default CSS white-space: normal collapses newlines.
trigger: An error with multi-line stack trace is caught and displayed.
impact: Developer/user troubleshooting is hindered by unreadable stack trace.
test_implication: Manual inspection of error display with a thrown Error will show stack as one line.
suggested_verification: Induce an error and inspect stack display in browser; observe lack of line breaks.
suggested_fix: Add `stackDiv.style.whiteSpace = 'pre-wrap';` or create a `<pre>` element and set textContent.

title: Unconditional display of stack trace can leak internal details
claim: The stack trace of any caught error is rendered into the DOM regardless of environment or debug flag, exposing internal file paths, function names, and code structure to end users, which is an information disclosure risk.
evidence: Catch block lines 32-37 create a div and set textContent to `e.stack` without checking `DEBUG` or production mode. The DEBUG flag at line 16 does not affect this.
impact: Potential leakage of sensitive implementation details.
test_implication: Security review should verify that stack traces are not shown in production; automated tests can assert error display does not contain stack in non-debug builds.
suggested_verification: In production build, trigger an error and observe if stack trace appears.
suggested_fix: Conditionally include stack trace only when DEBUG is true: `if (DEBUG) { const stackDiv = ... }` or use environment flag.

title: Error handler fails when caught value lacks a `stack` property
claim: If an exception is thrown that is not an Error object (e.g., `throw null` or `throw undefined`), the expression `e.stack` in the template literal will throw a TypeError, causing the error handling code to abort before displaying anything or logging to console.
evidence: `stackDiv.textContent = `Stack: ${e.stack}`;` assumes `e` is an object with a `stack` property; null/undefined have no properties.
trigger: Code somewhere throws null or undefined.
impact: The game's error handling fails, possibly leaving the UI blank and hiding the original error from developers.
test_implication: Unit test should simulate throwing non-Error values and verify error handling does not itself throw.
suggested_verification: Temporarily modify code to `throw null;` and observe console; current code will produce a new TypeError and not show error display.
suggested_fix: Use optional chaining and fallback: `stackDiv.textContent = `Stack: ${e && e.stack ? e.stack : 'No stack available'}`;` or `if (e instanceof Error) { ... }`.

title: Missing display:flex prevents commentary content from scrolling
claim: The #right-commentary-panel element is not a flex container, so its child #commentary-content with flex:1 and overflow-y:auto cannot scroll within the constrained panel height; content will be clipped by the parent's overflow:hidden.
evidence: Styles on #right-commentary-panel include `flex: 1 1 0; min-height: 0; overflow: hidden;` but no `display: flex; flex-direction: column;`. The child #commentary-content has `flex: 1; overflow-y: auto;` which only works if its parent establishes a flex formatting context and constrains its height.
trigger: When commentary content exceeds the available height of the panel, the content will be hidden because the parent clips it, and the child cannot scroll due to lack of a constrained height.
impact: Users cannot see all commentary; important game messages may be lost. The overflow hidden on parent makes the overflow-y:auto on child ineffective.
test_implication: Test by filling commentary content beyond panel height and verify scrolling works.
suggested_verification: Add `display: flex; flex-direction: column;` to #right-commentary-panel and ensure #commentary-content has `min-height: 0;`.
suggested_fix: Add `display: flex; flex-direction: column;` to #right-commentary-panel, and add `min-height: 0;` to #commentary-content to allow it to shrink and scroll.

title: Media query for max-width 600px fails to resize game container causing horizontal overflow
claim: In the 600px breakpoint, #game-container keeps its base width of 800px and height 600px, so on viewports narrower than 800px the container overflows horizontally.
evidence: Base rule: `#game-container { width: 800px; height: 600px; ... }`. Media query only changes `margin` and `padding` but does not override `width` or `height`.
trigger: Viewport width below 800px (e.g., mobile 600px or less) causes the container to be wider than the viewport, requiring horizontal scrolling and breaking layout.
impact: Poor mobile experience, horizontal scrollbar, content cut off, layout misalignment.
test_implication: Test on viewport widths around 600px, check for horizontal overflow.
suggested_verification: Set `width: auto;` or `width: 100%;` and adjust height (possibly `height: auto; min-height: 600px;`) within media query.
suggested_fix: Add `width: auto; max-width: 100%;` or `width: 100%;` and consider `height: auto;` in the media query.

title: Conflicting top and bottom positioning for #player-info in mobile media query
claim: In the max-width 600px media query, #player-info has both `top: 50%` (from base) and `bottom: 10px; left: 10px; right: 10px` (from media query), causing over-constrained positioning and likely misplaced panel.
evidence: Base rule sets `top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%);`. Media query adds `bottom: 10px; left: 10px; right: 10px;` but does not set `top: auto;` or remove `transform`. For absolutely positioned elements with both top and bottom set and height auto, the height is determined by the containing block minus top and bottom, but here top is percentage and bottom fixed, causing unpredictable layout.
trigger: Viewport width 600px or less, the player info panel will be stretched or mispositioned, likely overlapping other elements.
impact: Player information becomes unreadable or obscures game board, degrading usability.
test_implication: Test mobile layout; verify player info panel position.
suggested_verification: In the media query, set `top: auto; bottom: 10px; left: 10px; right: 10px; transform: none;` to anchor to bottom.
suggested_fix: Add `top: auto; transform: none;` to the #player-info rule inside the media query.

title: Ineffective mobile styles for dice container due to static positioning and min-height
claim: In the 600px media query, #dice-container sets `top: 10px; right: 10px;` but the element is not positioned (position static), so these properties have no effect; also width/height reduced to 50px but base `min-height: 60px` prevents height reduction.
evidence: Base #dice-container has no `position` property, default static, and `min-height: 60px`. Media query adds `top`, `right`, and sets `width: 50px; height: 50px` but min-height remains 60px, so used height is 60px, and top/right ignored.
trigger: On mobile view, dice container appears larger than intended and not repositioned.
impact: Layout may not optimize for small screens as intended.
test_implication: Verify dice container size and position on mobile.
suggested_verification: Inspect computed style on mobile; confirm actual height is 60px and top/right have no effect.
suggested_fix: Either add `position: relative;` or `position: absolute;` to #dice-container if repositioning is needed, and override `min-height: 50px;` in the media query.

title: Transition override on .game-token.move-to-board breaks left/top transitions
claim: The rule `.game-token.move-to-board { transition: transform 1.5s ease-in-out; }` overrides the base `.game-token` transition for left/top, so any left/top changes while the class is applied will not animate.
evidence: Base `.game-token` has `transition: left 250ms linear, top 250ms linear;`. The more specific `.game-token.move-to-board` sets `transition: transform 1.5s ease-in-out;`, replacing the entire transition property. If the token's position (left/top) changes while this class is active, the movement will be instant.
trigger: When a token moves to board with the class `move-to-board`, its left/top coordinates are likely updated, but due to missing left/top in transition, the movement snaps rather than animates.
impact: Smooth token movement is broken during a move-to-board animation, reducing visual quality.
test_implication: Test token movement animation; observe if left/top changes animate.
suggested_verification: Check if left/top properties are changed while the class is applied.
suggested_fix: Include left/top in the transition for `.game-token.move-to-board`, e.g., `transition: left 250ms linear, top 250ms linear, transform 1.5s ease-in-out;`

title: Duplicate #game-board-container definitions
claim: The selector #game-board-container is defined twice with conflicting properties: first `flex: 1 1 auto;` then later `flex: 1; position: relative;`. This is redundant and may cause confusion.
evidence: Lines: `#game-board-container { flex: 1 1 auto; }` and later `#game-board-container { flex: 1; position: relative; }`.
trigger: Future maintenance may modify one definition expecting it to be the only one, leading to unintended overrides.
impact: Increased risk of errors, unclear intention.
test_implication: None directly, but review CSS structure.
suggested_verification: Merge the definitions into one rule.
suggested_fix: Remove the duplicate or combine properties into a single #game-board-container rule.

title: Unsupported text-orientation: sideways may not render consistently across browsers
claim: The `text-orientation: sideways` property is experimental and not widely supported; without fallback, vertical text may appear in the wrong orientation.
evidence: Rule `.title-content { text-orientation: sideways; }` uses a value that is only supported in Firefox with flags or partial in others.
trigger: On browsers that do not support `sideways`, the text may default to `mixed` orientation, possibly not reading bottom-to-top as intended.
impact: Cosmetic issue with title panel display.
test_implication: Test on multiple browsers to verify title orientation.
suggested_verification: Check browser support; consider using `text-orientation: mixed` as fallback, and/or adding vendor prefixes if needed.
suggested_fix: Use `text-orientation: mixed` as fallback, and/or add -webkit- prefix for older Safari, or reconsider using writing-mode with rotation transforms.
